title: We Energies strikes deal to power Oracle data center with nuclear energy
key_facts: We Energies, a Wisconsin utility, announced on Friday 2 Oct 2026 an agreement that would let Oracle 'subscribe' to between 10% and 20% of the electricity generated at the Point Beach Nuclear Plant.
The power would help serve Project Lighthouse, a data center campus in Port Washington (Ozaukee County) that Oracle is co-developing with OpenAI.
The agreement still needs approval from the Wisconsin Public Service Commission (PSC).
If approved, We Energies spokesman Brendan Conway said it could spare the utility's other customers roughly $300 million in fuel costs over the next five years.
Point Beach (Manitowoc County) is Wisconsin's only operating nuclear plant and its largest generator, but its electricity costs more than alternatives, largely because of nuclear fuel costs.
We Energies sold the plant to NextEra Energy in 2007 but kept buying most of its output; it recently signed to keep buying about 86% for another 20 years (the current deal ends in 2033).
Separately, We Energies asked the PSC on Friday for approval to build a new natural gas plant at the Fox Energy Center site in Outagamie County, which would more than double the site's output.
quote_evidence: We Energies announced an agreement with the cloud computing giant on Friday that would allow Oracle to “subscribe” to between 10% and 20% of the Point Beach Nuclear Plant’s electricity generation.

The agreement still requires approval by Wisconsin’s Public Service Commission. If it is approved, We Energies spokesman Brendan Conway said it could spare the utility’s other customers roughly $300 million in fuel costs over the next five years.

Meanwhile, We Energies filed a separate application with the PSC on Friday seeking approval to build a new natural gas power plant on the site of the Fox Energy Center in Outagamie County. The proposed plant would more than double the site’s electricity output.
why_it_matters_hint: AI data centers are now claiming a share of an existing nuclear plant's output, and the utility says this could lower fuel costs for its other customers if regulators approve.
notes: Wisconsin Watch discloses that the OpenAI Foundation recently gave it a grant (OpenAI co-develops the Port Washington campus) and says it has no control over editorial decisions. The $300 million saving is the utility's own estimate and depends on PSC approval.
